summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Lamotte earned a doctorate at KU Leuven and studied in Rome and Paris under scholars including Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as chargé de cours at KU Leuven (1932–1974) and president at UCL (1950–1959).

Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he studied at Wellington College, earned a B.A. at Magdalene College (1938), and studied under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1949–1950). He also served in the Royal Artillery (1939–1941) and the Intelligence Corps (1941–1945).

Active in Buddhist studies, he studied at Fordham University (~1961–1965) and under Swami Satchidananda Saraswati and Chögyam Trungpa. He was executive vice president of Vajradhatu in 1973 and succeeded Trungpa in 1987.

A scholar of religious studies and Indology, Valk studied at Miina Härma Gymnasium and the University of Tartu (~1980–1986). He held a post at the University of Tartu around 1995 and served as an editor for Numen.
Active in Buddhist studies, Matsushima studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and later held a post there.
